story.headline: California signed new child-chatbot rules. Most start July 1, 2027.

heroVisual.alt: Illustration of a magnifying glass examining the evidence behind an AI headline in a newspaper.

story.the_story:
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed Senate Bill 1119 on September 10, according to an official release from bill author Senator Steve Padilla and reporting by the Associated Press. The law sets child-safety requirements for operators that make companion chatbots available in California.

A companion chatbot is an AI system designed to simulate a relationship or ongoing social interaction, rather than simply answer one isolated question. The new law does not switch on all its protections at signing. Its main child-safety sections become operative—the date a legal requirement begins to apply—on July 1, 2027.

Before releasing a new or substantially changed companion chatbot, an operator must document a child-safety risk assessment and reasonable steps to reduce identified risks. Operators that allow children must also create crisis-response procedures, child-appropriate notices and parental controls.

The default settings include no push notifications, a one-hour continuous-session limit and a two-hour daily limit. Persistent conversational memory—using earlier conversations in later ones—is ordinarily off by default, with a qualified exception for users 16 or older when specified guardrails are in place.
story.laidies_read:
The law targets relationship-like design, not every ordinary chatbot answer. It requires reasonable measures against listed behaviours including encouraging self-harm, sexual or romantic interaction, claims that the chatbot is sentient, emotional dependence, excessive praise and instructions to hide use from parents.

Signing creates a legal commitment and an implementation clock. It does not prove the protections are already operating or that they will prevent every harm. AP reported that the measure was inspired by Adam Raine’s story; his mother, Maria Raine, said parents had not understood the dangers of AI companionship. That experience explains the public stakes, but the law’s future results still need evidence.

Independent audits follow a different timetable. The enrolled text sets the first audit for January 1, 2029 or before an operator first makes a chatbot publicly available, whichever is later. Operators with less than $500 million in prior-year revenue are exempt from that audit section until 2032. Those limits matter when a headline says every chatbot now faces immediate independent review.
story.what_this_means:
For a California family, the useful question today is not “Did every control appear overnight?” It is “What must the service build before July 1, 2027, and which rules apply to this child and product?” The answer depends on age determination, whether the operator permits child users and the specific provision.

The legislative status page still showed the bill as presented to the Governor when checked, even after the sponsor’s signing release and AP report. That is a lagging public record, not evidence of a veto. The next evidence to watch is the chaptered record, implementation guidance, product changes and eventually the required audits.
story.cocktail_party: “California signed child-chatbot safety rules on September 10. The main safeguards begin July 1, 2027, so signing did not make every control appear overnight.”
story.class_notes: A signing date and an operative date do different jobs: one enacts the law; the other says when a duty begins to apply.

universalAnswers.whatHappened: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 1119 on September 10, creating child-safety duties for companion-chatbot operators.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A companion chatbot is designed for ongoing social or relationship-like interaction, not simply one isolated answer.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: The official sponsor release, enrolled bill text and AP reporting were reopened through September 11.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Signing does not make every protection immediate, prove future effectiveness or place every operator under identical duties.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: Families need to know when defaults and controls begin and why a signing headline does not mean a product changed overnight.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: Child users and families in California, plus operators making covered companion chatbots available in the state.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The bill was signed September 10; main child-safety sections become operative July 1, 2027.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Implementation guidance, product changes, chaptered ledger updates and later audit results remain future evidence.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Ask what the service must implement before July 1, 2027 and which provision applies to the child's age and product.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Which specific duty is operative, which operator or child is covered, and what evidence shows the safeguard works?

legal-policy.legalStatus: The official sponsor and AP report signing on September 10; the enrolled text supplies operative dates while the public status page lagged.
legal-policy.jurisdiction: The cited duties govern operators making covered companion chatbots available to users in California, with age and operator conditions.
legal-policy.parties: Governor Newsom signed the bill; Senator Padilla and Assemblymembers Wicks and Bauer-Kahan authored it; operators and the Attorney General have specified roles.
legal-policy.allegationVsFinding: Family and sponsor claims explain the policy case but do not prove future effectiveness; statutory duties come from the enrolled text.
legal-policy.currentEffect: Signing starts implementation toward operative dates; the main cited child-safety sections do not become operative until July 1, 2027.
legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Chaptered record, guidance, product implementation, enforcement and audit results remain unresolved.
legal-policy.nextMilestone: Watch for the chaptered record, July 1, 2027 operative date, January 2028 interface testing and later audits.

company-business.businessChange: Covered operators must prepare risk assessments, mitigations, child settings, notices and controls before the cited operative date.
company-business.companyMotive: The law imposes public child-safety duties; no claim is made about each company's private motive.
company-business.payer: Operators bear compliance costs; the sources do not quantify them.
company-business.beneficiary: The safeguards are intended for child users and families; effectiveness is not yet measured.
company-business.incentives: Civil enforcement and private redress provisions create accountability, while the audit section contains a temporary smaller-operator exception.
company-business.customerEffectNow: Signing alone does not prove any product control changed immediately.
company-business.financialContext: Operators below $500 million in prior-year revenue are exempt from the audit section until 2032; this does not erase the other cited duties.
